{{Short description|Relation used in the field of fluid dynamics}}
The '''Kozeny–Carman equation''' (or '''Carman–Kozeny equation''' or '''Kozeny equation''') is a relation used in the field of [[fluid dynamics]] to calculate the [[pressure drop]] of a [[fluid]] flowing through a [[packed bed]] of solids. It is named after [[Josef Kozeny]] and Philip C. Carman. The equation is only valid for [[creeping flow]], i.e. in the slowest limit of [[laminar flow]]. The equation was derived by Kozeny (1927)<ref name="Kozeny1927"/> and Carman (1937, 1956)<ref name="Carman1937"/><ref name="Carman1956"/><ref name="X">
{{Citation
  | title = Fluid Mechanics, Tutorial No. 4: Flow through porous passages
  | url = http://www.freestudy.co.uk/fluid%20mechanics/t4203.pdf
  }}
</ref> from a starting point of (a) modelling fluid flow in a [[packed bed]] as laminar fluid flow in a collection of curving passages/tubes crossing the [[packed bed]] and (b) [[Poiseuille's law]] describing laminar fluid flow in straight, circular section pipes.

==Equation==

The equation is given as:<ref name="X" /><ref name="A">
{{Citation
  | last1 = McCabe | first1 = Warren L.
  | last2 = Smith   | first2 = Julian C.
  | last3 = Harriot  | first3 = Peter
  | title = [[Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering]]
  | place = New York
  | publisher = McGraw-Hill
  | year = 2005
  | pages = 152–153
  | edition = seventh
  | isbn = 0-07-284823-5}}
</ref>
:<math>\frac{\Delta P}{L} = \frac{150 \mu}{\mathit{\Phi}_\mathrm{s}^2 d_\mathrm{p}^2}\frac{(1-\varepsilon)^2}{\varepsilon^3}V_\mathrm{0}</math>

where:
*<math>\Delta P</math> is the [[pressure drop]];
*<math>L</math> is the total height of the bed;
*<math>\mu</math> is the [[viscosity]] of the fluid;
*<math>\varepsilon</math> is the [[porosity]] of the bed (<math> \simeq 0.37 </math> for randomly packed spheres); <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wu |first1=Yugong |last2=Fan |first2=Zhigang |last3=Lu |first3=Yuzhu |date=2003-05-01 |title=Bulk and interior packing densities of random close packing of hard spheres |url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1023597707363 |journal=Journal of Materials Science |language=en |volume=38 |issue=9 |pages=2019–2025 |doi=10.1023/A:1023597707363 |s2cid=137583828 |issn=1573-4803|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
*<math>\mathit{\Phi}_\mathrm{s}</math> is the [[sphericity]] of the particles in the packed bed (<math>\mathit{\Phi}_\mathrm{s}</math> = 1.0 for spherical particles);
*<math>d_\mathrm{p}</math> is the diameter of the volume equivalent spherical particle;
*<math>V_\mathrm{0}</math> is the [[superficial velocity|superficial or "empty-tower" velocity]] which is directly proportional to the average volumetric fluid flux in the channels (q), and porosity (<math>\mathbf{\varepsilon}</math>). <ref name="B">
{{Citation
  | last1 = McCabe | first1 = Warren L.
  | last2 = Smith   | first2 = Julian C.
  | last3 = Harriot  | first3 = Peter
  | title = [[Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering]]
  | place = New York
  | publisher = McGraw-Hill
  | year = 2005
  | pages = 188–189
  | edition = seventh
  | isbn = 0-07-284823-5}}
</ref>
This equation holds for flow through packed beds with particle [[Reynolds number]]s up to approximately 1.0, after which point frequent shifting of flow channels in the bed causes considerable [[kinetic energy]] losses.

This equation is a particular case of [[Darcy's law]], with a very specific permeability. [[Darcy's law]] states that "''flow is proportional to the pressure gradient and inversely proportional to the fluid viscosity''" and is given as:

:'''q''' <math> = \frac{\kappa}{\mu} \frac{\Delta P}{L}</math>

Combining these equations gives the final Kozeny equation for absolute (single phase) permeability:

:<math> \kappa = \mathit{\Phi}_\mathrm{s}^2 \frac {\varepsilon^3 d_\mathrm{p}^2}{150(1-\varepsilon)^2} </math>

where:
*<math>\kappa</math> is the absolute (i.e., single phase) permeability.

== History ==
The equation was first<ref>Robert P. Chapuis and Michel Aubertin, "PREDICTING THE COEFFICIENT OF PERMEABILITY OF SOILS USING THE KOZENY-CARMAN EQUATION", Report EPM–RT–2003-03, Département des génies civil, géologique et des mines; École Polytechnique de Montréal, January 2003 https://publications.polymtl.ca/2605/1/EPM-RT-2003-03_Chapuis.pdf (accessed 2011-02-05)</ref> proposed by Kozeny (1927)<ref name="Kozeny1927">J. Kozeny, "[http://www.zobodat.at/pdf/SBAWW_136_2a_0271-0306.pdf Ueber kapillare Leitung des Wassers im Boden]." Sitzungsber Akad. Wiss., Wien, 136(2a): 271-306, 1927.</ref> and later modified by Carman (1937, 1956).<ref name="Carman1937">P.C. Carman, "Fluid flow through granular beds." Transactions, Institution of Chemical Engineers, London, 15: 150-166, 1937.</ref><ref name="Carman1956">P.C. Carman, "Flow of gases through porous media." Butterworths, London, 1956.</ref> A similar equation was derived independently by Fair and Hatch in 1933.<ref name="Fair1933"> G.M. Fair, L.P. Hatch, Fundamental factors governing the streamline flow of water through sand, J. AWWA 25 (1933) 1551–1565.</ref> A comprehensive review of other equations has been published.<ref name="Erdim2015"> E. Erdim, Ö. Akgiray and İ. Demir, A revisit of pressure drop-flow rate correlations for packed beds of spheres, Powder Technology Volume 283, October 2015, Pages 488-504 </ref>
